_about: Facade parts as data (v0.13). Sizes in metres. The generator (src/buildings.js, src/facade.js) reads these; weights are relative odds. Change a number here to change every house.

windows._about: Openings are cut through the wall and recessed: the frame and glass sit `recess` behind the wall face (v0.19: 26 cm, a thick stone wall), with a stone sill below. No lintel is drawn: the plaster runs to the edge of the opening, or a thin painted surround does (on decorated houses).
windows._columns: one window column per this many metres of wall (front = the wall on the house's lane)
windows._clearInFront: no openings or wall detail on a wall with a neighbour or the hillside closer than this in front
windows._sill: sill stone, picked per house: pale limestone to grey slate (ardesia)
windows._lintel: clear wall kept above an opening (no lintel is drawn since v0.19)
windows._surround: width of the painted band round an opening on decorated houses (m)

shutters._about: Two louvred leaves, each half the opening wide, hinged on the outer corner of the reveal: shut, they lie inside the reveal, `inset` behind the wall face; folded back, flat against the wall. Slats near the camera, a framed board far away. Each window draws a state; each leaf may also be faded (per house) .

states.name: open
states._: both folded back flat against the wall

states.name: half
states._: one shut, one standing part open

states.name: lost
states._: one leaf missing; the other shut or folded back

shutters._slatGap: share of each slat's height that is its shaded gap (drawn as a dark strip)
shutters._farPanel: far away a leaf is a framed board; its louvred panel is this much darker than the stiles
shutters._faded: share of houses whose shutters are sun-bleached, how far each leaf fades toward the bleached colour

balconies._about: Balconies on upper floors, mostly on the lane-facing (harbour-facing) wall. depth = how far the slab stands out.

groundFloors._about: What the ground floor of a house shows on its lane. `where`: harbour = by the harbour and piazza, town = elsewhere.

steps._: two stone steps at a house door: each this high; the lower one this much deeper

groundFloors._doorRise: a house door's threshold stands this far above the lane (two steps)

trim._about: Horizontal trim: a cornice under the eaves on every house, and on some a band at each floor line.

rhythm._about: What keeps the facades from looking stamped out (v0.21). Each house draws its own numbers from these ranges; windows still stack in vertical columns.
rhythm._storey: height of a house's ordinary storeys (m); the town's growth still counts 3 m a storey
rhythm._attic: share of houses whose top storey is a low attic, and its height
rhythm._tallFloor: share of houses with one storey of higher rooms, and by how much
rhythm._minGap: least plaster between two windows side by side (m)
rhythm._columnPitch: each house's window spacing, as a multiple of windows.columns
rhythm._centred: share of fronts whose window columns sit centred; on the rest they sit to one side
rhythm._window: each house's window size, as a multiple of the window type's
rhythm._oddColumn: share of houses with one column of narrower windows
rhythm._oddFloor: share of houses with one storey of shorter windows
rhythm._blankWall: share of side and back walls left without windows; chance that a painted window stands where one would have been
rhythm._sparseWall: share of the remaining side walls with a single column of windows
rhythm._cornice: the moulding under the eaves: two steps, one plain step, or none
rhythm._bands: a string course always runs along the front; chance it carries on round each other wall; share of houses where it stops part-way along the front, and where
rhythm._balconies: each house has this multiple of the usual balconies; chance a storey's balcony sits in the wall's own balcony column; chance it runs across the whole front
